question: Diagnose actual Experiment buying, checkout and stock-up evidence and its reported reasons. Distinguish cart actions, gifts, intentions, use, other-brand actions, remedies and adverse outcomes that coexist with loyalty.

count_definitions.experiment_acquisition_focal: Focal accounts explicitly narrating completed Experiment acquisition/checkout/stock-up. Exclude context-only accounts, metadata alone, use alone, gifts and other brands.
count_definitions.cart_readdition: Focal accounts explicitly returning an item to cart.
count_definitions.stockup_focal: Focal accounts explicitly stockpiling Experiment product.
count_definitions.routine_replacement_intended: Focal prospective product substitution in routine.
count_definitions.routine_replacement_completed: Focal explicit reported actual discontinuation/substitution in a routine. Functional redundancy (for example no more makeup remover needed) is retained separately but does not establish completed behavioral replacement.

method: Update your own initial findings using additions. Preserve still-supported findings and revise affected conclusions. Earlier sources remain retrievable by key if the prior findings are insufficient.

prior_findings.report:
Initial stage: Two focal accounts narrate completed Experiment acquisition: A04 describes four product categories and A05 one, totaling five product-action assertions. These are two credited retailer-review origins, not five buyers or a verified event count. Both support reported Experiment acquisition, but their particular buying reasons differ; no precise purchase motivation is independently repeated. No subsequent-stage evidence was supplied, so a second-stage diagnosis is unavailable.

A04 reports buying Super Saturated after a sister’s introduction and favorable experience, Buffer Jelly for greater nighttime hydration/repair, then face wash after the favorable Buffer Jelly experience, and mesh moisturizer immediately upon launch. The face wash and mesh descriptions align with Plasma Wash and Molecular Mesh, but exact SKUs/formulas are unconfirmed. Reported benefits include lightweight, fast-drying hydration before makeup, overnight glow, and cleanser-associated absence of breakouts and makeup removal. These are one actor’s sequential reports, not independently corroborated efficacy or causal effects. Attractive packaging is praised without explicit purchase attribution. Refill metadata does not establish repurchase. “No more makeup remover needed” establishes reported functional redundancy, not explicit completed routine substitution.

A05 explicitly checked out Avant Guard after TikTok creator discovery, in the context of sustainability concerns and having stopped sheet masks. Subsequent use includes imperfect cheek/nose fit, easy cleaning and motivation to use other hydrating products reported to help the skin barrier. Benefits cannot be assigned to the mask alone. The creator and sustainability context support this actor’s reported buying account, not a general causal claim.

A01 returned context-resolved Softwear to a cart because of a recommendation; no checkout, use or improvement is reported. A02’s aversion and habitual skipping concern the context-resolved Dr. Idriss exfoliator, alongside liking its baste balm; this is other-product scope. A12 acquired Regimen Lab cream 2.0 and cleanser, seeking a healing moisturizer after excessive tretinoin use. Positive experience motivates future exploration despite a cleanser-size complaint; none establishes Experiment acquisition.

Material context, excluded from focal counts: cowrunamuck (Reddit, September 5, 2025; score 21) explicitly reports two Softwear backups, attributing them to love of the balm and formerly harder access through direct shipping. They praise smoothness, moisture, sensitive-skin compatibility and absence of scent, prefer it to Eadem, and welcome Sephora availability. RowanVC (same thread/date; score 42) independently praises Softwear and Experiment generally; their unspecified lip-balm stash does not establish Experiment stockpiling. Their Dr. Idriss account describes tackiness and layering, often with lanolin, followed by soft lips. These distinct contextual actors repeat favorable Softwear appraisal within one community thread, but do not independently repeat the stock-up motive or supply A01 with purchase/use testimony. A02’s reply belongs to this same context, not a separate venue. Thread-opening questions resolve topic/brand only; their actor identities and engagement are unavailable.

Raw focal engagement: A01 score 13, A02 score 4, A12 score 12; all supplied as not interpreted/material_positive false. A04 and A05 each have 0 upvotes and 0 downvotes. Engagement observation times are unavailable. No resonance posture is awarded; scores cannot establish experience, independence, prevalence or buying effects. Reddit independence remains uncredited beyond visible distinct account identities; the two Junip origins are credited. Review updates are not additional origins or events.

Within the supplied initial set, no focal Experiment stock-up, gifted receipt, contemplated/completed return, or intended/completed routine substitution is explicit. No focal Experiment adverse outcome contradicts acquisition: A05’s fit limitation coexists with approval. A02’s aversion and A12’s size complaint concern other brands. The evidence supports bounded acquisitions and individual reported reasons; generalized repurchase, remedy-driven Experiment buying and market causation remain unestablished.

records.text:
Review title: Loved until it gave me dermatitis

Review body: I loved this product for the first few months until it gave me dermatitis. It was recommended by an influencer I follow and it was literally the best lip balm I had used up until then. My only gripe at the time was I would wake up in the morning with tons of dead skin on my lips, which I guess means it's doing its job, but I had to rub/brush the dead skin off every morning. I've seen reviews bashing the consistency which I kind of understand, it's very thick but I actually liked it and the sheen it left. Yes rubbing your lips together had resistance but I just didn't rub my lips together lol. Unfortunately I started getting perioral dermatitis from this product after a few months of use. My lips became so rough with tiny bumps and it got to the point where I had to get a steroid cream prescribed to me. After my lips were back to normal I tried it again hoping the dermatitis was caused by something else but my lips flared up within 24 hours worse than ever, so unfortunately it's confirmed caused by Softwear. I'm devastated because I loved it so much and I now have 3 unopened tubes I stocked up on during the months I loved it, there goes $70 CAD 😭. TL,DR: Definitely give it a try, the price is reasonable. But if you have sensitive lips, beware. I've never had a reaction like this in my life and my lips have never been sensitive so it really is a lottery of whether it'll do the same for you. I envy those who can use it 😭

Review title: Calming, Soothing, Buttery Soft Sorcery

Review body: For 100% transparency, I did receive this product free for an honest review at a later date but I've used it twice and needed to post this review here and now. This stuff is magical! Basically they took a barrier repair serum and a soothing, nourishing face oil and smooshed them together into this little dropper bottle to make a product that feels like someone's grandma crocheted the softest blanket ever just for your face. I really can't properly describe the texture. It does start out as a jelly-like substance that turns into a soft, fluidy oil as soon as it hits the skin. But where most oils seem to have a dryness or a taciness to them that make them feel disgusting while you're massaging them in, Buffer Jelly has a silky slip to it that just feels like heaven. I have rosacea and I've been adding a drop of this to my moisturizer at night and I wake up with super soft skin with no redness, irritation, or clogged pores. I think this will also be perfection for after dermaplaning. I was surprised by how small this bottle is when I first got it but I think it's simply deception due to Experiment using reduced packaging, because this is a full 1oz of product, which for an oil will last a VERY long time. So it's official, I'm an Experiment convert...

Review title: Confused

Review body: First, the texture is beautiful, it's so silky and plasma is the perfect descriptor for it! Unfortunately, I could not get a good cleanse out of this product, no matter how I used it. I tried a little bit (a quarter size), lathered in my hands, onto to wet skin; I tried the same on dry skin. I tried lathering on my face instead of in my hands first. I tried using a lot of product (2 quarters size), on wet face, on a dry face, lathering, not lathering... Every way I tried it didn't foam/bubble at all and almost seemed to be absorbing into my skin, it was disappearing. It was like rubbing a cream on my face that became more viscous after coming in contact with the water. That alone would not have been warranting of 2 stars, but this burned my eyes like no other cleanser I've used in a long time. I mean, badly, to the point I considered returning it. I don't really wear eye makeup ever so I just cleanse with my eyes closed, but boy was that a disappointment. Overall, this leaves my face feeling not as clean, and not as moisturized after one wash than my apparent all time fav cleanser(which is also a glycerin based cleanser, which is why I thought this one would be good for me). After two, it's just even drier feeling so I don't find it appropriate for a double cleanse. I'm unsure if I got a defective product somehow, or if I'm using the product wrong because I see so many great experiences from people on social media I'm genuinely confused...

Review title: Going into my lineup

Review body: Minimal and easy-to-use packaging. Very mild chemical smell to the product when dispensed. Nice light gel-serum texture and goes on with 0 sensitivity. (I actually hollered when I saw that it uses parabens for its preservative system—they’re the best preservatives!! So effective but also so well-tolerated and gentle. I think it speaks to the brand’s science-first approach to formulation and ingredients that they included them.) I currently use azelaic acid and salicylic acid products regularly so I think this product will probably replace both of those, which I like because I enjoy simplicity. My skin lovesssss salicylic acid and after using Continuum at night, I wake up with any active acne looking a bit less red than the night before. I can’t speak to how effective it really is at treating acne or post-acne pigmentation though because it’s hard for me to gauge something like that objectively. Overall I think this is a great product and will definitely be a new staple for me.
